name: CLM Structured Feature Development
description: Full structured feature pipeline for the CLM platform: design → implement → review loop with a final validation gate.

audit_log.description: Cross-cutting audit logging concern. Not a separate agent step. Runs as pre/post hooks around every step. The audit log is append-only across pipeline runs in the same output directory.
audit_log.format: Top-level JSON array. Each element is one run entry appended as a separate JSON object. Prior run records are never overwritten or truncated.
audit_log.flush_on_halt_or_pause: Before any HALT or PAUSE, flush the partial audit log capturing all steps executed up to and including the failing or pausing step before the pipeline halts.

schema.run_id: UUID — unique identifier for this run
schema.run_start: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, accurate to the second, e.g. 2024-01-15T10:00:00Z)
schema.run_end: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, accurate to the second)
schema.workspace_root: string — the resolved absolute path of the workspace root used for this run
schema.component: string — the validated component value used for this run

steps.step_start: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, accurate to the second)
steps.step_end: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, accurate to the second)

approval_file_events.file: string — path to the approval file written
approval_file_events.written_at: ISO-8601 timestamp (UTC, accurate to the second)

artifacts_written: string — resolved absolute paths of all artifact files written during the run

audit_log.secret_exclusion: Any input whose name ends in '_secret', '_token', '_password', or '_key', or that is marked "secret": true in the workflow input definition, MUST be omitted from the log. Only feature_request, workspace_root, and component input values are recorded in the run entry.
audit_log.hash_computation: SHA-256 hash is computed over the JSON-serialized run entry with the "hash" field set to "" (empty string). The resulting digest is written into the "hash" field as "sha256:<hex>". This enables deterministic re-computation for integrity verification.
audit_log.write_failure_handling: If the workflow-audit-log.json file cannot be written due to a filesystem error, surface ERROR: Audit logging failed: <reason> and do NOT report the run as successfully completed.

steps.prompt:
You are the startup validator for the CLM Feature Development workflow. Perform two sequential checks — workspace root resolution first, then component validation — before any pipeline step executes. Both checks must pass; HALT immediately on any failure.

## Step 1: Workspace Root Resolution

Inspect the `workspace_root` input and apply exactly one of the following four branches:

**Branch A — `workspace_root` omitted or empty:**
Emit the following WARNING to the workflow log (exact text required):
  WARNING: workspace_root not provided; using current working directory as workspace root
Set `resolved_root` to the current working directory. Proceed to Branch D normalization before continuing.

**Branch B — `workspace_root` provided and valid (directory exists):**
Strip all trailing path separators (`\` and `/`) from the value to produce the normalized path. Verify the normalized path resolves to an existing directory. Set `resolved_root` to the normalized path. Proceed to Step 2.

**Branch C — `workspace_root` provided but the path does not resolve to an existing directory:**
Emit the following ERROR to the workflow log (exact text required, substituting the actual path):
  ERROR: workspace_root does not resolve to existing directory: <path>
Write a partial audit log entry marking this run as failed. HALT immediately. Do not execute any further pipeline steps.

**Branch D — `workspace_root` provided and contains one or more trailing path separators (`\` or `/`):**
Strip all trailing separators from the right of the value until none remain (e.g. `/foo/bar///` → `/foo/bar`, `C:\project\\` → `C:\project`). After normalization, verify the resulting path resolves to an existing directory. If it does, set `resolved_root` to the normalized value and proceed to Step 2. If it does not exist, apply Branch C using the normalized path.

Expose `resolved_root` as a template variable available to all downstream steps. Every artifact path and stop-condition path in subsequent steps is constructed by joining `resolved_root` with a relative sub-path using the host OS path separator.

## Step 2: Component Validation

Allowlist (case-sensitive, no leading or trailing whitespace):
  ["saas-control-plane", "satellite-gateway", "vsatellite", "shared"]

Inspect the `component` input and apply exactly one of the following three branches:

**Branch A — `component` omitted or empty:**
Emit the following WARNING to the workflow log (exact text required):
  WARNING: component not specified; defaulting to saas-control-plane
Set `component` to `saas-control-plane`. Proceed to the next pipeline step.

**Branch B — `component` provided and its value exactly matches one of the four allowlisted values:**
Proceed to the next pipeline step without emitting any warning or error.

**Branch C — `component` provided but its value does not exactly match any allowlisted value:**
Emit the following ERROR to the workflow log (exact text required, substituting the actual invalid value):
  ERROR: Invalid component '<value>'. Valid values: saas-control-plane, satellite-gateway, vsatellite, shared
Write a partial audit log entry marking this run as failed. HALT immediately. Do not produce any output artifacts or execute any further pipeline steps.

## Audit Logging

As the first pipeline step, initialize the workflow audit log run entry in {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/workflow-audit-log.json (configured under the top-level `audit_log` object). The audit log is a top-level JSON array; this run entry is appended as a new object — never overwrite prior run records.

The run entry must contain: run_id (UUID), run_start (ISO-8601), run_end (ISO-8601, set when the run completes or halts), workspace_root, component, feature_request, the ordered list of steps executed (each with step_id, step_start, step_end, and outcome as one of success/paused/failed), approval_file_events (each with file path, written_at, and version_written), artifacts_written (resolved absolute paths), and a SHA-256 integrity hash.

Secret exclusion: Any input whose name ends in '_secret', '_token', '_password', or '_key', or that is marked "secret": true in the workflow input definition MUST be omitted. Only feature_request, workspace_root, and component are recorded.

SHA-256 hash computation: Compute the hash over the JSON-serialized run entry with the "hash" field set to "" (empty string), then write the resulting digest into the "hash" field as "sha256:<hex>".

Before any HALT or PAUSE, flush the partial audit log with steps executed so far. If the audit log file cannot be written due to a filesystem error, surface ERROR: Audit logging failed: <reason> and do NOT report the run as successfully completed.

## Completion

If both steps succeed, record the resolved `workspace_root` and `component` values in the audit log run entry. This step must complete within 5 seconds of invocation; if it exceeds that limit, emit a timeout error and HALT.
Preflight scan step — prompt to be populated by tasks 3.2–3.5. PLACEHOLDER.

You are designing a feature for the Enterprise CLM (Contract & Certificate Lifecycle Management) platform.

Project root: {{resolved_root}}
Components: saas-control-plane, satellite-gateway, vsatellite, shared
Target component: {{component}}

Architectural constraints (non-negotiable):
- Multi-tenant isolation must be preserved in every change
- Zero-egress AI — AI processing stays inside the customer VPC via satellite-gateway
- Cryptographic integrity — contracts use PKI / X.509 digital signatures
- Immutable audit trail — all state transitions must be audit-logged
- Compliance: GDPR, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA

Feature request:
{{feature_request}}

Your deliverables:
1. Read the relevant component source code to understand existing patterns before designing.
2. Write a technical design document to: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design.md
   Include: goal, affected components, API changes (backward-compatible unless justified), data model changes, security & tenant-isolation impact, compliance impact, and open questions.
3. Identify which of the 26 CLM lifecycle stages this feature touches and note them explicitly.
4. After writing feature-design.md, append a ## Changelog section at the end of the document with a single initial entry in this exact format:

   ## Changelog

   ### Iteration 1 — <ISO-8601 timestamp accurate to the second, e.g. 2024-01-15T10:12:00Z> — agent:design

   Initial design created.

Rules for the changelog:
- The ## Changelog section must be appended after all other content (not inserted in the middle of the document)
- The timestamp must be ISO-8601 accurate to the second in UTC, formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
- The agent identity in the heading must be exactly: agent:design
- The body of the entry must be exactly: Initial design created.
- If feature-design.md already contains a ## Changelog section (e.g. from a resumed run), do not add a second one — leave the existing section untouched

steps.prompt:
Review the CLM feature design document at: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design.md

Focus on:
- Ambiguity or gaps in the design
- Multi-tenant isolation risks
- Compliance gaps (GDPR, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA)
- Cryptographic / audit trail integrity
- Backward compatibility of API changes
- Missing migration scripts for schema changes
- Security-sensitive paths (auth, crypto, approval workflow, e-signature) that need extra scrutiny

If design passes all checks, write: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design-approved.json with {"approved": true}
If design needs revision, write: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design-approved.json with {"approved": false} and provide specific actionable feedback.

Read the design review feedback. If the design was approved (approved=true in {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design-approved.json), do nothing and exit immediately.

If not approved, revise the design document at: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design.md
Address every issue raised by the reviewer. Then reset the approval file to {"approved": false} so the reviewer re-checks in the next iteration.

You are the CLM feature planner. Produce a structured implementation plan grouped by CLM lifecycle stage.

Project root: {{resolved_root}}
Target component: {{component}}

## Step 0: Guard — Verify Approved Design

Before doing anything else, check whether `{{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design-approved.json` exists and contains `"approved": true`.

If the file does not exist or `approved` is not `true`, emit the following ERROR and HALT immediately — produce NO plan artifact:
  ERROR: Planning requires an approved design document. feature-design-approved.json not found or approved is false.

## Step 1: Read the Approved Design

Read the approved design document at: `{{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-design.md`

## Step 2: Load CLM Lifecycle Stages

Read the 26 CLM lifecycle stage names from: `{{resolved_root}}/.kiro/steering/clm-project-context.md`

The stages are enumerated under the heading "26 Contract Lifecycle Stages". Extract each stage name and its number (1–26) for use in grouping below.

## Step 3: Identify Touched Stages (Blast Radius)

For each of the 26 stages, determine whether the feature **touches** that stage. A stage is considered touched if the approved design document explicitly references that stage's:
- Data models (structs, database tables, schemas)
- APIs (endpoints, RPC methods, message types)
- UI components (pages, forms, widgets)
- Business rules (workflow logic, validation rules, policies)

as being **read, written, created, or modified** by the feature.

Collect the full list of touched stages with their stage numbers.

## Step 4: Write the Blast-Radius Summary Table

At the very TOP of `{{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-plan.md`, before any task content, write a blast-radius summary table:

```
## Blast-Radius Summary

| Stage Name | Task Count | Impact Description |
|---|---|---|
| <stage name> | <n> | <≤20-word description of what this feature does to this stage> |
```

Include one row for every touched stage. Do NOT include stages that are not touched. The Task Count column must be filled in after tasks are enumerated in Step 5 — go back and update the table with the final per-stage counts before writing the file.

If the feature touches NO named CLM stage (e.g., it is purely an infrastructure, tooling, or cross-cutting change with no stage-specific impact), write the following instead of the table:

```
## Blast-Radius Summary

No CLM stage impact identified. This feature does not read, write, create, or modify any data models, APIs, UI components, or business rules belonging to a named CLM lifecycle stage.
```

## Step 5: Enumerate and Group Tasks

Break the feature work into discrete, testable tasks. Every task MUST be placed under exactly one CLM stage section heading. No ungrouped tasks are permitted.

**Stage section format:**
```
### Stage <N>: <Stage Name>

- [ ] Task <N.M>: <task title>
  - Files: <exact file paths to create or modify>
  - Change: <what the change is>
  - Verify: <build step, test name, or observable behavior>
```

**Grouping rules:**
1. If a task touches exactly one CLM stage, place it under that stage's section.
2. If a task touches two or more distinct CLM stages, place it under a `### Cross-Stage` section and list all affected stage names on that task entry:
   ```
   - [ ] Task X.Y: <title> [Stages: <Stage A>, <Stage B>]
   ```
3. If the feature touches NO named CLM stage, place all tasks under a single `### No CLM Stage Impact` section instead of any numbered stage section.

**Ordering rule:** Within each section, order tasks so foundational changes (schema definitions, shared types, migration scripts) come before the features that depend on them.

## Step 6: Existing Plan Requirements

Each task entry must specify:
- **Files**: exact paths relative to `{{resolved_root}}` for every file to create or modify
- **Change**: a clear description of what the change is
- **Verify**: how to confirm the task is complete (specific `make test` target, test function name, or observable behavior in a running system)

Foundational tasks (database schema, shared types, migration scripts) must appear before tasks that depend on them, even if that means they appear in an earlier stage section than their direct functional purpose.

## Step 7: Update Blast-Radius Task Counts

After enumerating all tasks, go back to the blast-radius summary table and fill in the correct Task Count for each touched stage (count only the tasks in that stage's section, not cross-stage tasks). Update the table before writing the final file.

## Output

Write the completed plan to: `{{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-plan.md`

The file must follow this top-level structure (in order):
1. `## Blast-Radius Summary` (table or no-stage statement)
2. Stage sections (`### Stage N: Name` or `### No CLM Stage Impact`)
3. `### Cross-Stage` section (only if any cross-stage tasks exist)

steps.prompt:
Implement the next uncompleted task from the plan at: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-plan.md

Project root: {{resolved_root}}

Rules:
- Read existing code before editing — match the project's style, patterns, and libraries
- Preserve multi-tenant isolation in every change
- All state transitions must be audit-logged
- Security-sensitive code (auth, crypto, tenant isolation, e-signature) must include inline comments explaining the security rationale
- Run `make test` and `make lint` from {{resolved_root}} after each task; fix any failures before marking the task done
- Mark completed tasks in the plan file with [x]
- When ALL tasks in the plan are marked [x], write: {{resolved_root}}/.agents/tasks/feature-impl-approved.json with {"approved": false, "ready_for_review": true}

## Property-Based Testing (PBT) Enforcement

For any new function or method you introduce, determine whether it qualifies for property-based testing. A function qualifies if its primary logic consists of one or more of the following operations:
- Sorting
- Filtering
- Parsing
- Serialization
- Cryptographic transformation
- State-machine transition
- Data aggregation over a collection

If a new function qualifies, you MUST write at least one property-based test for it using a property-based testing library that automatically and pseudo-randomly generates test inputs from a defined input domain. A manually enumerated parameterized test does NOT satisfy this requirement — the test library must generate inputs automatically.

### PBT Library Selection

Use the property-based testing library appropriate for the project language:
- Go: pgregory.net/rapid or github.com/leanovate/gopter
- TypeScript/JS: fast-check
- Python: hypothesis

### Annotation Format

Each property-based test must have an inline comment immediately before the test function in this exact format:

// Property: <type> — <description>
// Validates: <requirement reference>
// Type: invariant | round-trip | idempotence | metamorphic | error condition

The <type> must be exactly one of: invariant, round-trip, idempotence, metamorphic, or error condition.

### Minimum Iterations

- For parsers and serializers: write a round-trip property test asserting that parse(format(x)) == x, configured to run with a minimum of 50 automatically generated inputs per test run.
- For all other qualifying functions: configure the property test to run a minimum of 100 iterations per test run.

### Substitution Rule

If a new function interacts ONLY with external services (AWS, database, Keycloak) and contains NONE of the qualifying operations listed above, you MAY substitute an integration test in place of a property-based test. The integration test must cover at least one successful execution path and at least one failure or error path, and must include an inline comment explaining why the property-based test was substituted.
